Fig. 1 Study flow chart. 347 patients with a 6-24 months old MRI confirming a lumbar disc herniation and pain in the lumbar region. 178 were excluded, because the new MRI revealed no new Modic changes or Modic type 2 changes only. 7 = refused participation, 3 wished to become pregnant and were advised against participation, 4 did not like the idea of long-term antibiotics. 162 patients were randomised: 45 took single dose antibiotics; 45 took double dose antibiotics; 36 took single dose placebo; 36 took double dose placebo. Both antibiotic arms join the antibiotic follow-up path: Drop outs = 13: 4 - side effects; 3 - new disc herniation; 1 - no show at follow-up; 2 - > 65 year of age; 1 - Modic 2; 2 - new cancer. 77 (85.6%) participated in 1 year follow-up. Both placebo arms join the placebo follow-up path: Drop outs = 5: 3 - new disc herniation; 2 - no show at follow up. 67 (93.1%) participated in 1 year follow-up.

proposed_results.relation_rationale: Select Table 3's continuous RMDQ endpoint at one year, pooled antibiotics versus pooled placebo, because it directly measures the requested disability construct and reports a complete main-comparison pair. RMDQ is first-named of two article primary measures (the other lumbar pain); no single designated primary outcome or hierarchy between these measures and timepoints is established by the original report. One year is the principal reported between-group comparison and current registry window. Table 3 reports medians 7.0 [4;11] versus 14.0 [8;18], p=0.0001; quartiles are not confidence intervals. No between-group effect estimate or CI is invented. This is narrower than the all-randomized assignment target because analysis is confined to one-year attendees. The 100-day RMDQ medians 11.5 versus 14.0 are an earlier competing window, and dose-specific 30% responder NNTs (4.0 and 3.0) change both endpoint and contrast and are not selected. Abstract 5.7 at one year and 11 at 100 days conflict with Table 3's 7.0 and 11.5; the abstract's statistic is not specified. Unknown which of crude t-test, age/sex-adjusted comparison or Mann-Whitney test produced the selected p-value. Registry currently labels a single conflated 'Low Back Pain Roland Morris Questionaire', not the article's two co-primary measures; it is dated augmentation, not historical registry bytes.

proposed_results.relation_rationale: The reported three-component first-event endpoint directly matches the requested clinical construct; the report explicitly includes silent MI. The proposed Result is the main reported stratified Cox hazard ratio, pooled semaglutide versus pooled placebo, on all randomized patients using the in-trial window planned through week 109, rather than a week-104 risk, on-treatment/per-protocol estimate, individual-dose comparison or programme-wide meta-analysis. The request specifies neither contrast, duration, analysis nor a designated primary result, so relation is related with unresolved scope facets pending approval rather than claiming all requested facets are known. Source-designated primary status is explicit in the report, final protocol, SAP and current registry; absence of a requester-designated primary result is not absence of source designation. Competing expanded composite adds revascularization and hospitalization (HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.62-0.89), while the all-cause-death composite changes the death component (HR 0.77; 95% CI 0.61-0.97); neither substitutes for the requested event set. The same numerical HR for the expanded endpoint and MI component does not establish equivalence. The selected HR derives from a stratified Cox model with pooled treatment fixed factor and randomization strata. P<0.001 concerns noninferiority with margin 1.8; the reported superiority P=0.02 was not prespecified or multiplicity adjusted.
